heading: Connecticut Paycheck Calculator

parts.markdown:
Use our free **Connecticut paycheck calculator** to estimate your take-home pay after federal income tax, Connecticut income tax, Social Security, Medicare and Connecticut Paid Leave contributions.

Enter your annual salary or hourly wage, select your payment frequency and provide your withholding information to see how much money you could receive on payday.

Whether you work in Hartford, Stamford, Bridgeport, New Haven or another Connecticut community, understanding your paycheck can help you evaluate employment opportunities and manage household expenses.

## How to Use the Connecticut Paycheck Calculator

If your pay stub lists Connecticut Paid Leave contributions, include the amount under other deductions. Enter each deduction once.

The calculator estimates employee earnings and deductions using your income and payroll information.

1. Select annual salary or hourly wages.
2. Enter your gross income before taxes.
3. Choose your payment frequency.
4. Enter the federal income tax withheld from that pay period.
5. Enter the Connecticut income tax withheld from the same pay period.
6. Include retirement contributions, insurance premiums and other deductions.
7. Review your estimated take-home pay.

Use the information from your latest pay stub and Form CT-W4 for a more representative estimate.

Employees with multiple jobs, interstate employment or irregular earnings may require additional calculations.

## How Connecticut State Income Tax Works

Connecticut applies progressive individual income tax rates. This means different portions of taxable income may be taxed at different rates.

For single filers and married individuals filing separately, the initial annual tax calculation uses the following brackets in 2026.

Other filing statuses use different thresholds.

Connecticut also applies personal exemptions, tax credits, phase-outs and tax recapture rules where applicable. Consequently, the bracket calculation alone may not determine your final income tax or paycheck withholding.

The [Connecticut withholding forms and publications](https://portal.ct.gov/DRS/DRS-Forms/Current-Year-Forms/Withholding-Forms) provide official calculation instructions.

## Understanding Connecticut Form CT-W4

Connecticut employees use Form CT-W4 to provide state withholding information to their employers.

Unlike the federal Form W-4, Connecticut uses letter-based withholding codes. The appropriate code depends on your expected filing status, household income and other circumstances.

For example, married employees whose spouses also work may need different withholding treatment from married employees in single-income households.

Employees qualifying for exemption from withholding may use the applicable exemption code.

Choosing an incorrect code can result in insufficient or excessive withholding throughout the year.

Review your CT-W4 after changing jobs, getting married or experiencing a significant change in household income.

## Connecticut Paid Leave Contributions

Connecticut Paid Leave provides financial benefits to eligible workers taking leave for qualifying family and medical circumstances.

In 2026, covered employees generally contribute 0.5% of eligible wages.

Assuming the annual contribution ceiling has not been reached:

The annual covered wage ceiling follows the Social Security contribution and benefit base.

For 2026, that limit is $184,500, giving a maximum standard annual contribution of $922.50.

Employees who reach the wage ceiling with an employer generally stop paying additional contributions through that employer for the remainder of the calendar year.

Approved private plans and certain employment arrangements may affect coverage.

Read the official [Connecticut Paid Leave contribution guidance](https://www.ctpaidleave.org/remit-contributions) for additional information.

## Connecticut Paid Leave Wage Limit Example

Suppose an employee has already earned $184,000 in covered wages and receives another $2,000 paycheck.

Only $500 remains below the annual contribution ceiling.

The contribution would be:

$500 × 0.005 = $2.50

Applying the contribution percentage to the entire paycheck would produce an incorrect deduction.

This is why entering year-to-date covered wages is particularly useful for higher-income employees.

Employees working for multiple employers may also need to review whether their combined contributions exceed the applicable annual limit.

## Federal Taxes Deducted From Connecticut Paychecks

Federal income tax withholding depends on your taxable income, payment frequency and federal withholding information.

Social Security generally deducts 6.2% of covered wages until the annual limit is reached.

For 2026, the annual Social Security wage limit is $184,500.

Ordinary Medicare withholding is 1.45% of covered wages.

Higher-income employees may encounter additional Medicare withholding when covered wages paid by their employer exceed $200,000 during the calendar year.

Employers use the federal calculation procedures described in [IRS Publication 15-T](https://www.irs.gov/publications/p15t).

## Connecticut Paycheck Example: $78,000 Salary

Suppose you earn $78,000 annually before taxes and deductions.
Assume your $3,000 biweekly paycheck is fully covered by ordinary payroll contributions and the annual limits have not been reached.

Approximately $2,755.50 remains before federal income tax, Connecticut income tax and other employee deductions.

Your actual take-home pay depends on the withholding information you provide to your employer.

## Connecticut Hourly Paycheck Calculator

Hourly employees can estimate gross earnings by combining regular pay and qualifying overtime.

Consider a worker earning $28 per hour who works 40 regular hours and five qualifying overtime hours at time-and-a-half.

Regular earnings: $28 × 40 = $1,120

Overtime earnings: $28 × 1.5 × 5 = $210

Total gross earnings: $1,330

Applicable taxes and contributions are then calculated from the relevant taxable wage amounts.

Employees receiving commissions, shift differentials or irregular bonuses should account for these separately where applicable.

Consult the [US Department of Labor overtime guidance](https://www.dol.gov/agencies/whd/overtime) for information about eligibility and exemptions.

## Working in Connecticut and Living in Another State

Connecticut's proximity to New York, Massachusetts and Rhode Island creates additional tax considerations for interstate commuters.

Employees may owe income tax in their work state while also having filing obligations in their residence state.

Resident tax credits may reduce double taxation, but eligibility depends on the applicable rules.

Remote work and employment across multiple states can complicate income sourcing.

Connecticut provides Form CT-W4NA for applicable nonresident wage apportionment situations.

A standard Connecticut paycheck estimate should not be treated as a complete interstate tax calculation.

## How Retirement and Health Benefits Affect Your Paycheck

Your employer may deduct contributions toward retirement savings, healthcare and other employee benefits.

Traditional 401(k) contributions generally reduce current federal income-taxable wages. Roth 401(k) contributions generally do not offer the same immediate tax reduction.

Qualifying health insurance arrangements may reduce certain taxable wages.

However, deductions do not necessarily affect income tax, Social Security, Medicare and paid leave contributions identically.

Review the taxable wage figures on your pay stub to determine how your employer classifies each deduction.

## Managing Your Connecticut Take-Home Income

Compare employment opportunities using estimated net earnings rather than annual gross salary alone.

Consider commuting expenses, housing costs, health insurance premiums and employer retirement contributions.

For employees commuting between Fairfield County and New York City, transportation expenses and interstate tax arrangements may significantly affect disposable income.

Use our [salary-to-hourly calculator](/calculators/salary-to-hourly-calculator/) to compare compensation arrangements and our [emergency fund calculator](/savings/emergency-fund-calculator/) to estimate the savings needed to cover unexpected expenses.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is Connecticut's income tax rate in 2026?

Connecticut uses progressive individual income tax rates ranging from 2% to 6.99%. Exemptions, credits, withholding codes and other adjustments affect the actual amount deducted from your paycheck.

### What is the CT Paid Leave deduction on my paycheck?

Covered employees generally contribute 0.5% of eligible wages, subject to the annual wage ceiling of $184,500 in 2026.

### Does Connecticut have municipal employee income taxes?

Connecticut municipalities generally do not impose a separate personal wage income tax. Federal income tax, Connecticut income tax and applicable payroll contributions still apply.
